title: Soul! Celestial in Thy Birth
description: Soul! Celestial in Thy Birth in Tonic Solfa to HEINLEIN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: These words were printed without an author's name in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 197, “Come Home!”, where the book credits them to Briggs' Collection.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7) (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to HEINLEIN; any other Sevens (7.7.7.7) tune fits them as well.
underlay: Soul! ce-les-tial in thy birth, Dwell-ing yet in low-est earth, Pant-ing, shrink-ing to be free, Hear God's spir-it whis-per thee.

lines: Thus it saith; in accents mild, —
"Turn to hope, and peace, and light,
Freed from sin, and earth, and night;
I have sought to make thee mine;
Still for thee good angels yearn;

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: anonymous words in print by 1848.
credits: Words anonymous, public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to HEINLEIN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
